title: the coronation planned
hook: the king says tomorrow, and tells his son a hard truth about hearts
carry: the hurry is where the danger lives

segments.voice: Yesterday: an old king asked his assembly, and the hall roared yes. Your line was he doesn't keep count.

Some decisions are made slowly and then, all at once, rushed: the plan everyone agreed on for months, suddenly happening this weekend, because someone got nervous. That's where Dasharatha is today. The assembly has said yes. The obvious next step is to set a good day, send the invitations, call Bharata home. Instead, the king sends for Rama twice in one day, and the second time his voice is urgent.
screen: `SLOW DECISION, SUDDEN RUSH.` → `SENT FOR TWICE IN ONE DAY.`

segments.voice: First Rama comes to his father's hall, bows, and hears the news in public. Keep up your good habits, the king tells him, and rule gently. Rama goes home. Then the charioteer Sumantra comes back for him: the king wants you again. This time Dasharatha speaks privately, and he sounds afraid. I've had bad dreams. Meteors have fallen with a crash. The astrologers say my star is under pressure from harsh planets, and when signs like this come, a king can lose his life, or fall into trouble. So the coronation will be tomorrow. Then he says something honest, and a little chilling. Do it now, while Bharata is away from the city. Bharata is good, he says, devoted to his elder brother, self-controlled, kind. But the minds of people change, even the minds of good people. The king isn't accusing anyone. He's admitting he doesn't trust time. Rama goes to tell his mother, Kausalya, who has been praying for exactly this. The king has already told him what the night requires, and the priest Vasishtha comes to Rama's house to see it done: tonight you and Sita keep a fast, and sleep on the ground, on a bed of sacred grass. Rama and Sita bathe, make an offering, and spend the night quietly in a shrine. The love is real. The plan is good. And the hurry is where the danger lives. A king who once asked a whole assembly for its opinion now wants it finished before his own son can come home.
screen: `RAMA HEARS IT IN PUBLIC.` · `BAD DREAMS AND FALLING STARS.` · `DO IT WHILE BHARATA IS AWAY.` · `A FAST ON SACRED GRASS.` · then, large: `THE HURRY IS WHERE THE DANGER LIVES.`

segments.voice: Notice if anything in you is rushing right now, a deadline, a reply, a decision you want over with, and name it to yourself in a few words. Then slow the breath on purpose, a little longer in and a little longer out, and let the plan wait the length of this sit.
Upavasa, the fast Rama and Sita keep the night before the rite. Shaken by omens, Dasharatha sets the coronation for tomorrow, while Bharata is away.
Your line: the hurry is where the danger lives. Even a good plan, rushed, can leave someone out. Day five hundred fifteen, done.

howItsDone: Fasting and keeping vigil the night before a major rite is a common Hindu practice; in the text, Vasishtha instructs Rama and Sita to fast and sleep on kusha grass before the consecration.

fork.setup: you're Dasharatha. the omens frighten you and the assembly has agreed. when do you crown Rama?
options: in a month, with every king invited.
fork.reveal: he says tomorrow, and tells Rama plainly: while Bharata is away, because even good minds can change.

original.note: Sanskrit upavāsa: a fast, literally staying near. Rama and Sita keep one the night before the rite.

trapdoor: what you thought: the coronation was planned slowly and carefully.
what it means: after a careful assembly, the king rushes it to the next day, afraid of omens.
what a scholar hears: readers have long argued about why the king wanted it done while Bharata was away; the text gives his fear of omens and of changing minds, and leaves the rest to us.

chat.says: If the whole assembly agreed, why did Dasharatha rush the coronation to tomorrow?
options: Bad omens scared him, and he wanted it done while Bharata was still away.
Rama asked him to hurry, so he could start ruling before the rains.
Bharata sent word asking him to finish it quickly, and not to wait for him.
chat.meaning: Shaken by bad dreams and falling meteors, Dasharatha set it for tomorrow, while Bharata was away, because even good people's minds can change.

upavasa.meaning: a fast, kept the night before a sacred rite

Sumantra.meaning: the king's charioteer, who fetches Rama a second time

Kausalya.meaning: Rama's mother, who has prayed for this day

Bharata.meaning: Rama's brother, away visiting his mother's family

recall: a vow kept for a purpose and a set time

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 3–4 (Rama summoned twice; omens; 'while Bharata is away')
Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 5–6 (Vasishtha's instructions; the fast and vigil)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
The omens (dreams, meteors, the king's birth-star afflicted by the sun, Mars and Rahu) are summarized; confirm.
Dasharatha's line that even good people's minds can change (Ayodhya 4): paraphrased; confirm.
upavāsa 'staying near' is the standard literal sense (upa + vas); confirm the note is acceptable.
